claim: Understanding how different neuronal types connect and communicate is critical to interpreting brain function and behavior.
source: Understanding how different neuronal types connect and communicate is critical to interpreting brain function and behavior.
evidence: This is a general statement about the importance of neuronal connectivity in neuroscience, representing established scientific consensus.

claim: It has remained a formidable challenge to decipher the genetic underpinnings that dictate the specific connections formed between neuronal types.
source: However, it has remained a formidable challenge to decipher the genetic underpinnings that dictate the specific connections formed between neuronal types.
evidence: This statement reflects the current state of the field as acknowledged in the scientific literature.

claim: The bilinear model transforms gene expressions of presynaptic and postsynaptic neuronal types into a covariance matrix.
source: Our model transforms the gene expressions of presynaptic and postsynaptic neuronal types, obtained from single-cell transcriptomics, into a covariance matrix.
evidence: This describes the methodology of the proposed model.

claim: The bilinear model achieved performance comparable to, if slightly better than, the spatial connectome model (SCM) in reconstructing electrical synaptic connectivity based on gene expressions in C. elegans.
source: When tested on a dataset of Caenorhabditis elegans, our model achieved a performance comparable to, if slightly better than, the previously proposed spatial connectome model (SCM) in reconstructing electrical synaptic connectivity based on gene expressions.
evidence: This claim is supported by the comparative analysis presented in the manuscript, including ROC-AUC scores.

claim: The bilinear model captured all genetic interactions identified by the SCM and inferred additional ones.
source: Through a comparative analysis, our model not only captured all genetic interactions identified by the SCM but also inferred additional ones.
evidence: This is supported by the comparative analysis of rule matrices using the discrepancy score metric.

claim: The bilinear model successfully recapitulated recognized connectivity motifs between bipolar cells and retinal ganglion cells in mouse retina.
source: Applied to a mouse retinal neuronal dataset, the bilinear model successfully recapitulated recognized connectivity motifs between bipolar cells and retinal ganglion cells
evidence: This is supported by the analysis showing alignment with kinetic attributes and polarity properties of retinal neurons.

claim: The bilinear model identified unique genetic signatures associated with different connectivity motifs, including genes important to cell-cell adhesion and synapse formation.
source: Specifically, it identified unique genetic signatures associated with different connectivity motifs, including genes important to cell-cell adhesion and synapse formation, highlighting their role in orchestrating specific synaptic connections between these neurons.
evidence: This is supported by the weight analysis of transformation matrices and GO enrichment analysis.

claim: Single-cell transcriptomics enables high-resolution profiling of gene expressions across neuronal types.
source: Single-cell transcriptomics enables high-resolution profiling of gene expressions across neuronal types (Zeng and Sanes, 2017; Stegle et al., 2015)
evidence: This is supported by citations to established literature on single-cell transcriptomics.

claim: Connectomic data offers detailed maps quantifying connections between neuronal cell types.
source: while connectomic data offers detailed maps quantifying connections between neuronal cell types (Denk and Horstmann, 2004; Helmstaedter et al., 2013; Tapia et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to established literature on connectomics.

claim: The challenge of linking gene expressions from single-cell transcriptomics to neuronal type connectivity from connectomic data has yet to be fully addressed.
source: However, the challenge of linking gene expressions derived from single-cell transcriptomics to neuronal type connectivity evident from connectomic data to uncover the genetic underpinnings has yet to be fully addressed.
evidence: This represents the gap in current research that the study aims to address.

claim: Bilinear models have been successful in capturing intricate user-item interactions in recommendation systems.
source: This model, in the context of recommendation systems, has been successful in capturing intricate user-item interactions (Koren et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to literature on recommendation systems.

claim: The bilinear model revealed additional genetic interactions beyond those uncovered by the SCM when applied to C. elegans data.
source: Notably, it revealed additional genetic interactions beyond those uncovered by the SCM.
evidence: This is supported by the comparative analysis of rule matrices.

claim: The bilinear model provides biologically meaningful insights into candidate genes and genetic interactions that orchestrate connectivity between bipolar cells and retinal ganglion cells.
source: The model not only unveils connectivity motifs between BCs and RGCs but also provides biologically meaningful insights into candidate genes and the genetic interactions that orchestrate this connectivity.
evidence: This is supported by the gene signature analysis and GO enrichment analysis.

claim: The bilinear model predicts potential BC partners for RGC transcriptomic types, with predictions aligned substantially with functional descriptions from previous studies.
source: Furthermore, our model predicts potential BC partners for RGC transcriptomic types, with these predictions aligned substantially with functional descriptions of these cell types from previous studies.
evidence: This is supported by comparison with functional annotations from Goetz et al., 2022.

claim: Synaptic specificity is a meticulously orchestrated process that underpins the functionality of neural networks.
source: This specificity is not a mere coincidence but a meticulously orchestrated process that underpins the functionality of the entire network (Sanes and Zipursky, 2020; Martin et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to literature on synaptic specificity.

claim: Different types of bipolar cells form specific synaptic connections with various types of retinal ganglion cells in the retina.
source: A classic example of chemical synaptic specificity is observed in the retina, where different types of BCs form specific synaptic connections with various types of RGCs (Helmstaedter et al., 2013; Euler et al., 2014; Sanes and Masland, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to literature on retinal connectivity.

claim: Specific gap junction connections have been observed between C. elegans neurons.
source: Meanwhile, specific gap junction connections, composed of connexins in vertebrates and innexins in invertebrates, has been observed between C. elegans neurons (Kumar and Gilula, 1996; Phelan et al., 1998; Rabinowitch and Schafer, 2015; Marcus et al., 2014; Südhof, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to literature on C. elegans gap junctions.

claim: The genetic principles guiding the formation of specific synaptic connections in complex brain structures remain elusive.
source: The genetic principles guiding the formation of these specific connections, particularly in complex brain structures, remains elusive.
evidence: This represents the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Kaufman et al. showed a correlation between gene expression of C. elegans neurons and their connectivity.
source: For instance, Kaufman et al. showed a correlation between gene expression of C. elegans neurons and their connectivity (Kaufman et al., 2006)
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Varadan et al. developed an entropy minimization approach for understanding the molecular logic of synaptic connectivity in C. elegans.
source: and Varadan et al. developed an entropy minimization approach for understanding the molecular logic of synaptic connectivity in C. elegans (Varadan et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Early models did not fully account for spatial constraints for synaptic formation.
source: These models, however, did not fully account for spatial constraints for synaptic formation.
evidence: This is a critique of prior models based on their methodological limitations.

claim: The SCM correlates gene expression of neurons with their connectivity via a rule matrix.
source: Specifically, the SCM in Kovács et al. correlates the gene expression of neurons with their connectivity via a rule matrix.
evidence: This describes the methodology of the SCM from prior research.

claim: The SCM restricts analysis to neuron pairs that are in physical contact.
source: By restricting the analysis to neuron pairs that are in physical contact, the SCM transforms the original problem into a regression between the Kronecker product of the gene expression matrix and an edge list that captures neuronal connectivity (Kovács et al., 2020).
evidence: This describes a key feature of the SCM methodology.

claim: Taylor et al. introduced network differential gene expression analysis (nDGE), a statistical method that examines co-expression of gene pairs between neuron pairs.
source: Additionally, Taylor et al. introduced the network differential gene expression analysis (nDGE), a statistical method that expands upon traditional differential gene expression analysis by examining the co-expression of gene pairs between neuron pairs, comparing synaptic versus non-synaptic neuronal groups through t-tests.
evidence: This describes the nDGE methodology from prior research.

claim: nDGE operates as a mass-univariate method, focusing on single gene pairs' contributions without considering complex interactions among multiple co-expressed genes.
source: Unlike multivariate methods such as the SCM, nDGE operates as a mass-univariate method, focusing on single gene pairs' contributions to synaptic formation without considering the complex interactions among multiple co-expressed genes.
evidence: This describes a methodological characteristic of nDGE.

claim: The generalization of SCM and nDGE models to neuronal cell types has not been explored.
source: While the SCM and nDGE models have focused on the connectivity of individual neurons and were tested using C. elegans datasets, their generalization to neuronal cell types has not been explored.
evidence: This identifies a gap in prior research.

claim: Bilinear models capture the interaction between users and items via low-dimensional latent features in recommendation systems.
source: Bilinear models capture the interaction between users and items via low-dimensional latent features (Koren et al., 2009; Rendle et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to literature on recommendation systems.

claim: The bilinear model can assign different weights to gene expressions of pre- and post-synaptic neurons, enabling capture of heterogeneous interactions.
source: One key advantage of the bilinear model is its capacity to assign different weights to the gene expressions of pre- and post-synaptic neurons, enabling the model to capture not just homogeneous but also complex, heterogeneous interactions fundamental to understanding neuronal connectivity.
evidence: This describes a methodological advantage of the bilinear model.

claim: Prior studies have highlighted heterogeneous interactions in synaptic connections, noting formation of connections between pre- and post-synaptic neurons expressing different cadherins.
source: Prior studies have highlighted such heterogeneous interactions, noting the formation of connections between pre- and post-synaptic neurons expressing different cadherins, indicative of a heterogeneous adhesion process (Duan et al., 2014; Duan et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to literature on cadherin-mediated synaptic connections.

claim: The bilinear model achieved a ROC-AUC score of 0.6435 in reconstructing C. elegans gap junction connectivity.
source: From the calculation, the bilinear model achieved a ROC-AUC score of 0.6435, slightly surpassing the SCM's score of 0.6428.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the model evaluation.

claim: The SCM achieved a ROC-AUC score of 0.6428 in reconstructing C. elegans gap junction connectivity.
source: From the calculation, the bilinear model achieved a ROC-AUC score of 0.6435, slightly surpassing the SCM's score of 0.6428.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the model evaluation.

claim: Both the bilinear model and SCM scores are substantially distant from the ideal score of 1, suggesting that innexin expression data alone is insufficient for fully capturing gap junction connectivity in C. elegans.
source: However, it is noteworthy that both scores, while above 0.5, are substantially distant from the ideal score of 1. This observation suggests that relying exclusively on innexin expression data might be insufficient for fully capturing the detailed gap junction connectivity in C. elegans.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the quantitative results.

claim: The Pearson correlation coefficient between the bilinear model's rule matrix and the SCM's rule matrix is 0.90 (p < 0.001).
source: Visualization of the two matrices suggests a high degree of similarity between them, which is quantitatively supported by a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.90 (p < 0.001), underscoring a strong alignment.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the comparative analysis.

claim: The bilinear model identified certain innexins (inx-11, inx-8, inx-5, and inx-2) as implicated in co-expression patterns within connected neurons.
source: certain innexins (inx-11, inx-8, inx-5, and inx-2) were implicated in co-expression patterns within connected neurons
evidence: This is a result from the analysis of the bilinear model's rule matrix.

claim: The bilinear model identified certain innexins (inx-11, inx-9, inx-3, inx-5, inx-7) as associated with an avoidance pattern, suggesting lack of co-expression in neuron pairs forming gap junctions.
source: while another set (inx-11, inx-9, inx-3, inx-5, inx-7) was associated with an avoidance pattern, suggesting a lack of co-expression in neuron pairs forming gap junctions.
evidence: This is a result from the analysis of the bilinear model's rule matrix.

claim: The Pearson correlation between the reconstructed connectivity matrix and the connectomic data for mouse retinal neurons is 0.83 (p < 0.001).
source: The resulting correlation of 0.83 (p < 0.001) demonstrated a robust association between the transformed gene expression features and the connectomic data.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the model evaluation on mouse retinal data.

claim: Only 9 out of 115 connections in the target matrix were not represented in the reconstructed matrix for mouse retinal neurons.
source: Notably, the analysis revealed that only a small fraction, specifically 9 out of 115 connections, were not represented in the reconstructed matrix.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the discrepancy analysis.

claim: The optimal number of latent dimensions for the mouse retinal dataset is two.
source: Our cross-validation procedure indicated that the optimal number of latent dimensions was two (Figure 4—figure supplement 1; see 'Methods and supplementary materials' for details).
evidence: This is a result from the cross-validation procedure.

claim: The two latent dimensions capture connectivity motifs that align with kinetic attributes (transient versus sustained responses) and polarity (ON versus OFF responses) of retinal neurons.
source: Interestingly, these distinct connectivity motifs align with two widely recognized properties of retinal neurons: kinetic attributes that reflect the temporal dynamics (transient versus sustained responses) of a neuron responding to visual stimuli, and polarity (ON versus OFF responses) reflecting whether a neuron responds to the initiation or cessation of a stimulus (Euler et al., 2014; Sanes and Masland, 2015; Masland, 2012; Baden et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the latent dimensions supported by comparison with known retinal neuron properties.

claim: The first latent dimension emphasizes connectivity patterns between BCs and RGCs that laminate within the IPL's central region and marginal region.
source: The first dimension appeared to emphasize connectivity patterns between BCs and RGCs that laminate within the IPL's central region, as well as those that laminate within the marginal region (Figure 5a, d and g).
evidence: This is supported by visualization of connectivity reconstructed using only the first latent dimension.

claim: The second latent dimension emphasizes connections between BCs and RGCs that laminate within the outer and inner regions of the IPL.
source: Notably, the spotlight shifted to connections between BCs and RGCs that laminate within the outer and inner regions of the IPL, respectively (Figure 5b, e and i).
evidence: This is supported by visualization of connectivity reconstructed using only the second latent dimension.

claim: Genes like CDH11 and EPHA3 carried high weights for BCs forming synapses in the IPL's central region in the first latent dimension.
source: In the first latent dimension, genes like CDH11 and EPHA3, involved in cell adhesion and axon guidance, carried high weights for BCs forming synapses in the IPL's central region.
evidence: This is a result from the weight analysis of the transformation matrices.

claim: PCDH9 and UNC5D carried high weights for BCs synapsing in the marginal region in the first latent dimension.
source: In contrast, for BCs synapsing in the marginal region, we observed high weights in the cell adhesion molecule PCDH9 and the axon guidance cue UNC5D (Figure 6a).
evidence: This is a result from the weight analysis of the transformation matrices.

claim: PCDH7 carried high weights for RGCs forming synapses in the IPL's central region in the first latent dimension.
source: For example, in RGCs forming synapses in the IPL's central region, the cell adhesion molecule PCDH7 carried high weights
evidence: This is a result from the weight analysis of the transformation matrices.

claim: PCDH11X and CDH12 were associated with high weights for RGCs synapsing in the marginal region in the first latent dimension.
source: whereas for RGCs synapsing in the marginal region, cell adhesion molecules PCDH11X and CDH12 were associated with high weights (Figure 6b).
evidence: This is a result from the weight analysis of the transformation matrices.

claim: Guidance cues SLIT2, NLGN1, EPHA3, and PLXNA4, and adhesion molecule DSCAM were assigned high weights for BCs laminating in the IPL's outer region in the second latent dimension.
source: For BCs laminating in the IPL's outer region, high weights were assigned with guidance cues such as SLIT2, NLGN1, EPHA3, and PLXNA4, as well as the adhesion molecule DSCAM.
evidence: This is a result from the weight analysis of the transformation matrices.

claim: CNTN5 was associated with high weight for BCs in the inner region in the second latent dimension.
source: For BCs in the inner region, the adhesion molecule CNTN5 was associated with a high weight (Figure 6c).
evidence: This is a result from the weight analysis of the transformation matrices.

claim: PLXNA2, SLITRK6, PLXNA4, CDH8, and LRRC4C were associated with high weights for RGCs forming synapses in the IPL's outer region in the second latent dimension.
source: In RGCs, we noticed that guidance molecules such as PLXNA2, SLITRK6, and PLXNA4 along with adhesion modules CDH8 and LRRC4C were associated with high weights for cells forming synapses in the IPL's outer region.
evidence: This is a result from the weight analysis of the transformation matrices.

claim: SDK2 was among the top genes for RGCs laminating and forming synapses in the IPL's inner region in the second latent dimension.
source: In contrast, the adhesion molecule SDK2 was among the top genes for RGCs laminating and forming synapses in the IPL's inner region (Figure 6d).
evidence: This is a result from the weight analysis of the transformation matrices.

claim: Plexins (PLXNA2, PLXNA4) are known to play crucial roles in establishing specific synaptic connections.
source: Some of these genes or gene families, such as Plexins (PLXNA2, PLXNA4), Contactin5 (CNTN5), Sidekick2 (SDK2), and Cadherins (CDH8,11,12), are known to play crucial roles in establishing specific synaptic connections (Matsuoka et al., 2011; Sun et al., 2013; Peng et al., 2017; Krishnaswamy et al., 2015; Duan et al., 2014; Duan et al., 2018; Liu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to literature on synaptic connectivity genes.

claim: Contactin5 (CNTN5) is known to play crucial roles in establishing specific synaptic connections.
source: Some of these genes or gene families, such as Plexins (PLXNA2, PLXNA4), Contactin5 (CNTN5), Sidekick2 (SDK2), and Cadherins (CDH8,11,12), are known to play crucial roles in establishing specific synaptic connections (Matsuoka et al., 2011; Sun et al., 2013; Peng et al., 2017; Krishnaswamy et al., 2015; Duan et al., 2014; Duan et al., 2018; Liu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to literature on synaptic connectivity genes.

claim: Sidekick2 (SDK2) is known to play crucial roles in establishing specific synaptic connections.
source: Some of these genes or gene families, such as Plexins (PLXNA2, PLXNA4), Contactin5 (CNTN5), Sidekick2 (SDK2), and Cadherins (CDH8,11,12), are known to play crucial roles in establishing specific synaptic connections (Matsuoka et al., 2011; Sun et al., 2013; Peng et al., 2017; Krishnaswamy et al., 2015; Duan et al., 2014; Duan et al., 2018; Liu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to literature on synaptic connectivity genes.

claim: Cadherins (CDH8,11,12) are known to play crucial roles in establishing specific synaptic connections.
source: Some of these genes or gene families, such as Plexins (PLXNA2, PLXNA4), Contactin5 (CNTN5), Sidekick2 (SDK2), and Cadherins (CDH8,11,12), are known to play crucial roles in establishing specific synaptic connections (Matsuoka et al., 2011; Sun et al., 2013; Peng et al., 2017; Krishnaswamy et al., 2015; Duan et al., 2014; Duan et al., 2018; Liu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to literature on synaptic connectivity genes.

claim: Delta-protocadherins (PCDH7,9,11x) emerged as new candidates potentially mediating specific synaptic connections.
source: Others, particularly delta-protocadherins (PCDH7,9,11x), emerged as new candidates potentially mediating specific synaptic connections (Sanes and Zipursky, 2020).
evidence: This is a prediction from the model analysis, with citation to literature on protocadherins.

claim: GO enrichment analysis revealed two common themes among top genes: neuronal development and synaptic organization.
source: Intriguingly, when we listed the top 10 significant GO terms for each latent dimension based on their adjusted p-values, we found two common themes: neuronal development and synaptic organization (Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is a result from the GO enrichment analysis.

claim: About 47% of the top genes identified by the model are involved in neural development and synaptic organization.
source: Supplementary file 4 also highlights the number of the top genes associated with each GO term, revealing that overall about 47% of these genes are involved in neural development and synaptic organization.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the GO enrichment analysis.

claim: Eight out of ten predictions of BC partners for transcriptionally defined RGC types aligned with functional descriptions from Goetz et al., 2022.
source: Among the ten predictions made, eight aligned with these functional descriptions, lending support to the predictive power of our model.
evidence: This is a result from the validation of model predictions against functional annotations.

claim: The bilinear model's computational complexity is considerably more manageable than the SCM, offering scalability as dataset sizes increase.
source: In contrast, the computational demands of our bilinear model, driven primarily by matrix multiplication in gradient descent, are considerably more manageable, offering scalability and feasibility even as dataset sizes increase.
evidence: This is a methodological comparison based on computational complexity analysis.

claim: The modest ROC-AUC scores for C. elegans gap junction connectivity reconstruction suggest that additional molecular mechanisms beyond innexin interactions play crucial roles in forming specific electrical synaptic connections.
source: In assessing the bilinear model's and the SCM's performance to reconstruct C. elegans gap junction connectivity, the resulting modest ROC-AUC scores (approximately 0.64, much lower than the ideal 1.0) underscore the challenges in predicting electrical synapse specificity using innexin expressions alone. This suggests that additional molecular mechanisms, beyond innexin interactions, play crucial roles in forming specific electrical synaptic connections.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the quantitative results.

claim: Research on the C. elegans motor circuit has revealed how a developmental program fine-tunes cAMP signaling to guide neuron-specific assembly of electrical synapses.
source: For instance, research on the C. elegans motor circuit has revealed how a developmental program fine-tunes cAMP signaling to guide neuron-specific assembly of electrical synapses (Palumbos, 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citation to literature on C. elegans electrical synapse assembly.

claim: The observed coexistence of electrical and chemical synapses in close proximity intimates potential shared mechanisms underlying their specificity.
source: Furthermore, the observed coexistence of electrical and chemical synapses in close proximity intimates potential shared mechanisms underlying their specificity (Lasseigne et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citation to literature on synapse coexistence.

claim: Plexins A4 and A2 (PLXNA4, PLXNA2) have been shown to be necessary for forming specific lamina of the IPL in the mouse retina.
source: For instance, Plexins A4 and A2 (PLXNA4, PLXNA2), predicted to be crucial for RGCs' synapsing in the outer IPL, have been shown to be necessary for forming specific lamina of the IPL in the mouse retina, interacting with the guidance molecule Semaphorin 6 A (SEM6A) (Matsuoka et al., 2011; Sun et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to literature on Plexins in retinal development.

claim: Contactin5 (CNTN5) has been shown to be essential for synapses between ON BCs and the ON lamina of ON-OFF direction-selective ganglion cells.
source: Contactin5 (CNTN5), which our model predicted as vital for BCs forming synapses in the inner IPL, has been shown to be essential for synapses between ON BCs and the ON lamina of ON-OFF direction-selective ganglion cells (ooDSGCs; Peng et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to literature on Contactin5 in retinal connectivity.

claim: Sidekick2 (SDK2) has been shown to guide the formation of a retinal circuit that detects differential motion.
source: Sidekick2 (SDK2), predicted to be critical for RGCs' synapses in the inner IPL, has been shown to guide the formation of a retinal circuit that detects differential motion (Krishnaswamy et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to literature on Sidekick2 in retinal circuits.

claim: Cadherin combinations have been implicated in synaptic specificity within retinal circuits.
source: Similarly, Cadherins (CDH8,11,12), whose combinations have been implicated in synaptic specificity within retinal circuits (Duan et al., 2014; Duan et al., 2018), were highlighted for multiple connectivity motifs.
evidence: This is supported by citations to literature on Cadherins in retinal connectivity.

claim: Cadherin8 (CDH8) has been shown to be guided by the transcriptional factor Tbr1 for laminar patterning of J-RGCs.
source: In particular, Cadherin8 (CDH8), which our model predicted to be crucial for RGC's synaptic connections in the outer IPL, has been shown to be guided by the transciptional factor Tbr1 for laminar patterning of J-RGCs, a type of OFF direction-selective RGCs (Liu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to literature on Cadherin8 in RGC development.

claim: Mutations in delta-protocadherins in mice and humans have been linked with various neurological phenotypes, including axon growth and guidance impairments and changes in synaptic plasticity and stability.
source: While their roles in synaptic connectivity aren't fully understood (Sanes and Zipursky, 2020), mutations in delta-protocadherins in mice and humans have been linked with various neurological phenotypes, including axon growth and guidance impairments and changes in synaptic plasticity and stability (Kahr et al., 2013; Light and Jontes, 2017; Peek et al., 2017; Bisogni et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to literature on delta-protocadherins.

claim: The bilinear model missed several connections among specific BC-RGC pairs such as those between RGC types 51, 5ti and BC types 3a, 3b, and 4.
source: Secondly, the model, despite its overall success in reconstructing the connectivity matrix, missed several connections, notably among specific BC-RGC pairs such as those between RGC types 51, 5ti and BC types 3a, 3b, and 4 (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a limitation identified through the discrepancy analysis.

claim: The list of top genes identified by the model is enriched with genes directly mediating synapse formation and maintenance, such as adhesion molecules.
source: Finally, the list of top genes identified by our model is enriched with genes directly mediating synapse formation and maintenance, such as adhesion molecules (Figure 6; Supplementary file 4)
evidence: This is a result from the gene signature analysis and GO enrichment analysis.

claim: The model overlooks transcription factors like Tbr1 known to affect synaptic specificity.
source: yet overlooks transcription factors like Tbr1 known to affect synaptic specificity (Liu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a limitation identified through comparison with known biology.

claim: The connectivity matrix was deduced from stratification profiles derived from EM reconstruction.
source: Firstly, the model's connectivity matrix was deduced from stratification profiles derived from EM reconstruction.
evidence: This describes the source of the connectivity data used in the study.

claim: Stratification is a meaningful indicator of connectivity within the mouse retina, as certain BC types preferentially connect with specific RGC types stratified in the same lamina.
source: Although prior research has indicated stratification as a meaningful indicator of connectivity within the mouse retina, as certain BC types preferentially connect with specific RGC types stratified in the same lamina (Duan et al., 2014; Krishnaswamy et al., 2015; Duan et al., 2018)
evidence: This is supported by citations to literature on retinal connectivity.

claim: Stratification may not capture the entire complexity of synaptic connections.
source: this metric may not capture the entire complexity of synaptic connections (Dunn and Wong, 2014).
evidence: This is a limitation acknowledged with citation to literature.

claim: The weight matrix ensures that the model does not disproportionately favor neuronal types with a greater number of neurons over rarer types.
source: As our study focuses on the genetic code of pre- and post-synaptic neuronal types rather than individual neurons, this weight matrix ensures that the model does not disproportionately favor neuronal types with a greater number of neurons over rarer types.
evidence: This explains the rationale for the weighting scheme in the model.

claim: PCA can be performed on gene expression vectors to reduce multicollinearity by removing components with negligible eigenvalues.
source: To mitigate this, we can perform principal component analysis (PCA) on the gene expression vectors, transforming them into a new coordinate system and removing components with negligible eigenvalues to reduce redundant information.
evidence: This describes a methodological approach to address multicollinearity.

claim: Regularization techniques such as L2 regularization (Ridge) or L1 regularization (Lasso) can be applied to manage multicollinearity.
source: Alternatively, we can apply regularization techniques, such as L2 regularization (Ridge) or L1 regularization (Lasso) to effectively manage the multicollinearity.
evidence: This describes methodological approaches to address multicollinearity.

claim: The bilinear model adopts a simplifying assumption that connectivity and latent gene expression features of individual cells can be approximated by the averages of their corresponding cell types.
source: To tackle this issue, we adopt a simplifying assumption that the connectivity and latent gene expression features of individual cells can be approximated by the averages of their corresponding cell types.
evidence: This describes a key assumption of the model when dealing with data from different sources.

claim: The bilinear model can facilitate the anticipation of synaptic partners for newly characterized transcriptional types within a neural region.
source: Trained on data from a specific neural region, the bilinear model can facilitate the anticipation of synaptic partners for newly characterized transcriptional types within that region, thereby generating hypotheses on their functional roles within neural circuits.
evidence: This describes a potential application of the model.

claim: The bilinear model can be used to predict changes in synaptic partners resulting from genetic manipulations.
source: Furthermore, this model opens avenues for inferring neural wiring alterations resulting from genetic manipulations. For instance, by altering the genetic profile of certain neuronal types to create new transcriptionally defined types, we can use the model to predict changes in their synaptic partners, offering insights into the consequent reconfiguration of neural networks.
evidence: This describes a potential application of the model.

claim: The bilinear model could be extended to hypothesize the rewiring of the brain under psychological disorders such as autism.
source: This could be further extended to hypothesize the rewiring of the brain under psychological disorders, such as autism, where significant connectome changes suggest shifts in synaptic partner choices (Roine et al., 2015; Hong et al., 2019).
evidence: This describes a potential application of the model with citations to literature on autism connectomics.

claim: The bilinear model holds significant potential for elucidating the genetic underpinnings of neuronal connectivity across various species and brain regions.
source: Our bilinear model, while illustrated using the C. elegans and mouse retina datasets, holds significant potential for elucidating the genetic underpinnings of neuronal connectivity across various species and brain regions, contingent upon the availability of comprehensive gene expression profiles and synaptic connection data.
evidence: This describes the potential generalizability of the model.

claim: A comprehensive single-cell transcriptome atlas for the adult fruit fly brain has been established.
source: For instance, the advent of a comprehensive single-cell transcriptome atlas for the adult fruit fly brain, alongside the recent establishment of its complete connectome, offers a fertile ground for extending our model to decipher the complex neural circuits of Drosophila (Davie et al., 2018; Ding et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citations to literature on Drosophila transcriptomics and connectomics.

claim: The complete connectome of the adult fruit fly brain has been recently established.
source: For instance, the advent of a comprehensive single-cell transcriptome atlas for the adult fruit fly brain, alongside the recent establishment of its complete connectome, offers a fertile ground for extending our model to decipher the complex neural circuits of Drosophila (Davie et al., 2018; Ding et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citations to literature on Drosophila transcriptomics and connectomics.

claim: Single-cell sequencing efforts have unveiled a rich tapestry of transcriptomic cell types across cortex regions and the hippocampus in the mouse brain.
source: In the context of the mouse brain, the depth and breadth of single-cell sequencing efforts have unveiled a rich tapestry of transcriptomic cell types across cortex regions and the hippocampus (Tasic et al., 2016; Tasic et al., 2018; Yao et al., 2021; Yao et al., 2023a).
evidence: This is supported by citations to literature on mouse brain transcriptomics.

claim: The scalability of the bilinear model supports the prospect of its cross-regional application in the brain.
source: The scalability of our bilinear model, akin to collaborative filtering's effectiveness in e-commerce domains, supports the prospect of its cross-regional application.
evidence: This is an inference about the model's potential based on its computational properties.

claim: Future research will explore adaptations of the model to datasets that combine single-cell transcriptomic profiling with long-range neuronal projection mapping.
source: To address this, future research endeavors will also explore adaptations of our model to other available datasets, such as those that combine single-cell transcriptomic profiling with long-range neuronal projection mapping (Chen et al., 2019; Sun et al., 2021).
